Source: Principles of Correct Practice for Guitar
Author: Jamie Andreas
Why It Matters: Defines attention, tension, correct practice, and how the body learns. This should shape the simulator voice and failure-recovery design.
First Extraction Scope: Printed pages 13-27, 33-40, 69-77; then right hand and left hand sections.
Output To Build: Practice principles source notes; Foundation body-scan and first-sound lesson support

Author: Aaron Shearer
Why It Matters: Gives a disciplined beginner technique path: positioning, tone, rest stroke, free stroke, left hand, and efficient movement.
First Extraction Scope: TOC plus printed pages 1-27 and 29-42 first.
Output To Build: Foundation technique map; source support for rest/free stroke interaction

Author: Bill Edwards
Why It Matters: Provides a pattern-based fretboard model. This can anchor Study once Foundation has begun.
Output To Build: Fretboard map source notes; Study node concept graph

Author: Marc Schonbrun
Why It Matters: Text-readable theory source for glossary, misunderstood-word prevention, and Study node sequencing.
First Extraction Scope: TOC, fundamentals, rhythm, scales, chords, key signatures, intervals.

Author: K. Anders Ericsson
Why It Matters: Gives scientific grounding for deliberate practice, feedback, expert development, and visible intervals to mastery.
First Extraction Scope: Introduction, deliberate practice/expert performance chapters, learning environment design sections.
Output To Build: Hearth learning-science notes; Practice design principles for Martin

Source: The Cambridge Handbook of Expertise and Expert Performance
Author: K. Anders Ericsson et al.
Why It Matters: A deeper reference for learning science and cross-domain simulator design, especially useful beyond guitar.
First Extraction Scope: Do not process end to end. Pull selected chapters only after the practice model is clearer.
Output To Build: Research backing for reusable simulator engine and progress model

Author: Aniruddh D. Patel
Why It Matters: Supports the core idea that music can be understood through language-like learning and brain development.
First Extraction Scope: Overview chapters and rhythm/language/music cognition sections.
Output To Build: Hearth explanation notes; music-as-language framework support

Source: This Is Your Brain on Music
Author: Daniel J. Levitin
Why It Matters: Already source-noted. Good for learner-facing explanations about sound, memory, emotion, anticipation, taste, and expertise.
First Extraction Scope: Already mapped at chapter level; deepen only when Hearth lessons need it.

Author: Patrick Stefurak
Why It Matters: Text-readable beginner source that can support the practical sequence after the philosophical spine is stable.
First Extraction Scope: Practice planning and early beginner concept sequence.

Author: Mark Phillips & Jon Chappell
Why It Matters: Already source-noted. Useful for turning concepts into small, practical beginner tasks.
First Extraction Scope: Already partially source-noted; deepen around first chords and finger independence when needed.
Output To Build: Doing drills and Foundation action steps
